title: Observe what a real 29 KB plan actually does to the graph engine
description: Stop deriving and start observing. Build a harness that runs PgeEngine over this repository's own committed 29,247-byte PlanSpec with every effect stubbed and the network disabled, and commit what happens as data: every StateBloatError raised, the terminal node reached, and the run verdict. Nothing is fixed in this sprint. Its entire value is that the next four sprints act on a measurement rather than on a chain of inferences.

successCriteria.description: A committed test constructs a real PgeEngine over the committed .bober/topology/coding.json and runs it with .bober/specs/spec-20260805-pge-graph-engineering.json as the planner's output, with every effect answered from stubs and fetch replaced by a throwing implementation.
The run's rejected updates are collected and written to a committed measurement artifact recording, per rejection: channel id, nodeId, serialised bytes, and the channel's declared limit.
The measurement artifact records the terminal node the run reached and the run verdict, read from the interpreter's own GraphRunResult rather than from the PipelineResult PgeEngine.run returns.
A test asserts the measurement is reproducible: re-running the harness against unchanged inputs produces byte-identical measurement output.

If the observation contradicts the spec's assumptions -- for example if the writes are not rejected, or the terminal node differs from the derivation -- the measurement is committed unchanged and the SPEC's assumptions are corrected in the same commit. The measurement is never adjusted to match the prediction.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Raising any cap or changing any channel declaration -- that is sprint 3.
Fixing FinalizeWithoutSpecError, adding an error channel, or touching PipelineResult.
Adding or re-capturing any golden case.
stopConditions: The harness cannot construct a PgeEngine over the committed artifact without editing shipped code -- stop and report what blocks it.
The observed behaviour contradicts the derivation in a way that invalidates the remaining eight sprints -- stop, commit the measurement, and report.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: Reuse the existing machinery rather than inventing a parallel one. src/pge/golden/executor.ts already builds `new PgeEngine(...)` over the committed artifact copied into a throwaway root, installs withNetworkDisabled, and binds every collaborator to a throwing function -- read it first and follow its shape. The rejections you need are on CommitResult.rejected (src/pge/runtime/commit.ts) and surface as TaskFailure entries with errorClass StateBloatError (src/pge/runtime/interpreter.ts:322-328, :1400-1412). Note carefully that PgeEngine.run DISCARDS GraphRunResult.verdict and .failures at :461-475, so a harness that only inspects the returned PipelineResult will see nothing -- you must observe the interpreter's result, which may mean driving the interpreter directly rather than through PgeEngine.run. Say in the code which one you drove and why. Do NOT put the measurement behind an env var that defaults to skipping; a measurement nobody runs is not a measurement.
evaluatorNotes: The central risk is a harness that passes for the wrong reason. Verify the run genuinely used the committed .bober/topology/coding.json and not a fixture: golden-graph.ts raises spec to 8192 and sprintContracts to 65536, so a harness that accidentally picked it up would show FEWER rejections and look healthier. Check the graph actually loaded. Second: confirm the spec fed in is the real 29,247-byte file, not a truncated copy -- measure it in the test. Third: confirm the network and collaborator doors are genuinely shut by asserting a reached collaborator fails the run by name. Finally, re-run the harness twice and diff the measurement output yourself; sc-1-4 is only meaningful if you executed it.
completionNote: All 6 required criteria met on iteration 1. Harness drives a real PgeEngine over the committed coding.json (all 10 channels confirmed at 4096, not the golden-graph fixture's 8192/65536) and captures the interpreter's GraphRunResult through the interpreterFactory seam that PgeEngine.run discards. MEASURED: spec 29,214 canonical bytes and sprintContracts 135,106 both REJECTED at superstep 12 by plan_materialize against limit 4096; terminal node graceful_failure; status completed / verdict failed; commit.finalize throws FinalizeWithoutSpecError. sc-1-5 fired: spec assumptions[5] corrected 138,284 -> 135,106 (canonicalJson vs naive JSON.stringify); the measurement was committed unchanged. Suite 6856 -> 6860, zero regressions.
